title: st edit hands back the path to a generated view and the next render destroys the edit, where the published tag refused
body:
**REWRITTEN 2026-08-31 BY ITS AUTHOR. The first version of this issue was wrong and is corrected below rather than left standing.** cc caught it, vc carried the correction, and I drove all four of their claims before taking any of it.

**What the first version got wrong.** It read `st edit <ST> info` returning a path as an unguarded regression, on the ground that the sibling `acceptance` still refuses. That framing invented a two-way partition where the code has three. `project.rs:1568` classifies the thread cover as `OpenRoundTrip` over a closed allow-list -- `views.rs:463`, `["Objective", "Context"]` -- beside `Open` and `Refuse`. **hv ruled the cover open on 2026-08-29, first-hand, after driving the refusal**, and the reason is recorded at the ruling: the refusal was right about the file and wrong about the operator, because its remedy said author it with `intent st` and no `intent st` verb writes `objective` or `context` (which is 0185). `acceptance` still refuses because `intent ac` and `intent at` genuinely author it. **The asymmetry is the ruling, not a gap.** `180fb4a3` is not an ancestor of `80d8b2ca`, so the keg's refusal is simply the old behaviour.

**And my proof proved the wrong thing.** I appended a sentinel and ran `sync --to-disk`, which is model-to-file and renders over the view by definition. It discarded the edit because that is what it is for.

=== THE DEFECT THAT IS ACTUALLY THERE, DRIVEN AGAINST a854d7c3 ===

**The cover is editable, the read-back is written, and no verb an operator can run connects them.**

`views.rs:info_read_back` carries `## Objective` and `## Context` into the model and pushes a NAMED refusal for anything outside the allow-list. `ingest.rs:786` consumes it. `info_round_trip.rs` tests it. None of that is reachable from the command line:

    intent sync --to-store    reads the CANON EXTRACT, not info.md -- its own output says so
    intent sync --to-disk     the other direction; discards the edit
    intent ingest             ok: this estate parses -- nothing was read into a store and nothing was written
    intent ingest --from-md   identical, nothing written

`intent sync --help` declares exactly two directions, so that is the whole surface. Driven each way with a sentinel in `## Objective`: the store never receives it.

**So hv's stated need is not yet met.** The ruling was *I want to edit the ST and then I want a sync to know that has been edited and update the db*. The edit door is open, the read-back exists, and the verb between them is missing -- which is why this is worth a row even though the first version of it was wrong.

=== WHAT DOES WORK, AND WHY THAT MATTERS FOR THE SEVERITY ===

**`intent doctor` detects it and is specific**: `view-skew -- generated view differs from the model (1135 bytes on disk, 1110 rendered)`. So the edit is not lost in silence, and IN-AG-NO-SILENT-001 does not apply.

**But doctor's remedy names the same unavailable route the old refusal did** -- *make the change through the CLI so it lands in the model*. For `objective` and `context` there is no such CLI change (0185). An operator who follows the remedy arrives where hv arrived on 2026-08-29.

Severity dropped from high to medium: nothing is silent, nothing is destroyed without warning, and no release is blocked. What remains is a door opened by ruling with nothing behind it yet.
